paragraphs.source_en: The repainting of Round Head figures is very frequent in the Tassili especially with the large enigmatic figures which were probably considered particularly important. This could have been the case for the figures at Uan Bender. This shelter is hidden inside a stone city on a high hill and virtually impossible for a herd of cattle to reach. Pastoralists could have only come here without their animals to make the paintings and they would have only done so if they considered the place important. As it was also a significant shelter for the hunters, it is likely that they would refresh their paintings when they were covered by the other culture's figures. Obviously, the paintings may have been refreshed by an individual or group other than that who created them, perhaps as a sign of a continuity of cults.
